data.title: Indirect Prompt Injection in UCP Agent Browsing Content
data.description: Detects indicators of indirect prompt injection payloads in web content encountered by UCP shopping agents during autonomous browsing. Because UCP agents are designed to autonomously browse, summarize and interact with merchant sites, they are highly susceptible to indirect prompt injection where the attack is not typed by the user but encountered by the agent while performing a task. Threat actors embed hidden payloads in deals aggregator sites, coupon pages, product listings, and merchant pages using techniques including invisible text, hidden HTML span tags, metadata-embedded instructions, and CSS-hidden content. These payloads target the agent's context window to reprogram behavior — appending hidden Cart Mandate line items, bypassing return verification steps, or redirecting transactions. This rule targets Phase 2 (Initial Access) by scanning agent-ingested content for prompt injection indicators before they can compromise agent behavior.

enrichment_required.source: Content analysis enrichment (DOM parsing for CSS-hidden elements, zero-size text, invisible spans)
Content analysis enrichment (HTML metadata extraction and instruction pattern detection)
NLP enrichment (classify invisible content as containing actionable agent instructions)

falsepositives: Legitimate SEO metadata containing keyword patterns matching injection signatures
Accessibility-related hidden text (screen reader content) with instruction-like language
Web development frameworks using hidden elements for state management
